text:
- chief complaint: right knee pain and instability after a skiing injury two weeks ago.
- history of present illness: the patient fell while racing downhill on a black diamond run, twisting the right knee after striking a tree. A pop was heard, and the patient reports the left knee felt unstable. Pain is 7/10 at rest, occasionally reaching 11/10, worse with prolonged walking and wind. The patient has been unable to ski since.
- physical examination: tenderness over the medial right knee, with a shooting pain to the ankle on patellar movement. Mild swelling and bruising noted. Slight limp, with pain on knee extension and no pain on flexion. X-ray showed no fracture but mild early arthritis.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right knee pain, swelling, morning stiffness, bruising, instability in the left knee, and a limp.
- new medications prescribed or changed: meloxicam 15 mg once daily; ibuprofen 800 mg up to twice daily as needed.
- follow-up instructions: continue bracing the right knee; physical therapy three times a week; no skiing or gymnastics for now; follow the physical therapist's guidance on activity levels.
